exceptions.reason: Arranges the "variable is absent" precondition before capture so the test can prove dispose restores absence rather than an empty string.
exceptions.rationale: The scope cannot arrange the state a scope is asked to restore. These writes happen before CaptureAsync (to build the "absent" / "empty string" preconditions) or after DisposeAsync (to hand the process back what it had before the test began), so by construction they cannot be routed through the scope. Nothing about a future refactor removes them.

exceptions.reason: UseCulture sets the current culture; this is the write the mutator exists to own.
exceptions.rationale: This is the audited primitive itself: GlobalTestStateScope is where the repo has decided every process-global write belongs, so the writes it performs cannot be migrated anywhere else without dissolving the mechanism. Registering them keeps the file inside the gate — a Thread.Sleep or a new static added here still fails the check, because the allowlist entry covers only StaticSetter on this path.

exceptions.reason: The poll interval of the bounded observation window, awaited on the injected TimeProvider and cancelled by the window token — a paced re-observation, not a sleep-before-assert.
exceptions.rationale: BoundedObservationWindow is the bounded-polling primitive that Eventually and Consistently are built on, and this Task.Delay is its poll interval. It is the bottom of the wait stack: the advice "replace the delay with Eventually" terminates here, so there is nothing to migrate to and no date to set. The allowlist entry covers only Task.Delay on this path.
